Major (x2), all five absence allowlists null: fixed, not left for P7. The lists are an inventory of what this site's own build emits, read off its 435 pages; no kit numbers were copied. inlineScripts: the JSON-LD and the graph data, each pinned to its data type, so the same opening in classic code is unnamed. externalScripts: the search payload, the 3 moved Starlight classics, the 4 upstream modules (reason: alive over HTTP, inert from a folder) and the Expressive Code script. mainStylesheet: _astro/style.*.css. otherStylesheets: print and ec. noscriptStyles: the exact Head.astro line (NOSCRIPT_STYLE), and a real-tree test holds it equal to Head.astro. An unnamed script, a remote script, a second main stylesheet, an unnamed stylesheet, inline classic code, a changed noscript selector and a missing noscript all now fail with the add-or-stop repair; each is planted in check-site-absence.test.ts. I re-ran the verifiers' probes on a copy of the real dist and every one fails. The null/Tally-note path is gone. New `needs` field: an entry for something only some sites carry (graph data, the ec assets) is owed only when the file that signals it is built; tested both ways.

The root decision is listed under open.

New Allowed.needs field (not in the spec). An entry for something only some sites carry names the built file that makes it owed, so a small site with no graph page or code block does not fail the unused-entry check. The ec stylesheet is tied to the ec script, because Expressive Code writes its stylesheet on every build.
Inline allowlist entries carry a `type` and match only a script of that type. This is stricter than the spec's body-opening match.
